welcomeMessage: This website is provided as a public service by the Hillsborough Police Department. In an effort to protect victim privacy, this website does not provide information regarding juvenile offenders, or specific information regarding calls for service that are sensitive in nature. The Hillsborough Police Department does not guarantee the accuracy, completeness, or timeliness of the information contained on this website regarding specific incidents, crimes, or people with respect to the omission of information that may have not yet been filed or is pending filing with a court of jurisdiction relating to criminal offenses. With regards to the people listed on the arrest page, arrests shown on that page are generated by arrests entered into the Records Management System at the Hillsborough Police Department and do not reflect all arrests in San Mateo County.
missingPersonsText: The Hillsborough Police Department is requesting your assistance in finding the individuals listed. If you have any information regarding their location, please contact the Hillsborough Police Department at 650-375-7470
stolenVehiclesText: Please do not take direct action if you see any of the stolen vehicles listed. If you see one of the vehicles listed please contact the Hillsborough Police Department at 650-375-7470 or call 9-1-1.
arrestText: Using this website, members of the public will have access to public information regarding individuals arrested by the Hillsborough Police Department. Unless otherwise declared “guilty” or “convicted”, arrestees are considered innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.
securityCameraDisclaimer:
The Hillsborough Police Department security camera registry allows resident owners to voluntarily register their security cameras with the Hillsborough Police Department. Police will not have access to the camera systems, but will be aware that a camera exists when investigating a crime in or around their neighborhood.


If a crime occurs in the vicinity of a registered surveillance camera, investigators may use the provided contact information to request surveillance footage. Camera footage may include the actual crime, or an escape route which can provide descriptive information that can lead to the identification and ultimately the prosecution of a suspect.
securityCameraAdditionalInfoInstructions: Please include any additional information regarding your cameras. (Do they face the street, do you have access to the footage 24 hours a day, are you able to provide a copy of the footage to the police department, etc.)
securityCameraSuccessText: Thank you for submitting your camera information. If you need to change any information, please submit another form or call the station directly 650-375-7470.
crimeStatsDisclaimer: Crimes reported to the Hillsborough Police Department as defined by the FBI for the National Incident Based Reporting System (NIBRS) program.
stopDataStatsDisclaimer: Demographic information is based on the officer's personal observation and initial perception only. This information is not solicited from the person stopped or obtained from the person's driver's license or other identification. The information reported may not reflect the demographic information on the person's identification or how the person identifies.
stopDataStatsDefinitions:
• “Reason for Stop” refers to the primary reason why the officer stopped the person.
    • Traffic violation
    • Reasonable suspicion that the person was engaged in criminal activity
    • Probable cause to arrest or search
    • Probable cause to take into custody under Welfare and Institutions Code section 5150
    • Known to be on parole/probation/PRCS/mandatory supervision
    • Knowledge of outstanding arrest warrant/wanted person
    • Investigation to determine whether the person is truant
    • Consensual encounter resulting in a search
  • “Perceived Race or Ethnicity of Person Stopped” refers to the officer’s perception of the race or ethnicity of the person stopped. When reporting this data element, the officer shall make their determination of the person’s race or ethnicity based on personal observation only. The officer shall not ask the person stopped their race or ethnicity, or ask questions or make comments or statements designed to elicit this information. Officers may report one or more of the following options for the person stopped:
    • Asian
    • Black/African American
    • Hispanic/Latine(x)
    • Middle Eastern or South Asian
    • Native American
    • Pacific Islander
    • White
  • “Perceived Gender of Person Stopped” refers to the officer’s perception of the person’s gender. When reporting this data element, the officer shall make their determination of the person’s gender based on personal observation only. The officer shall not ask the person stopped their gender or use the gender specified on the person’s driver’s license or other identification, recognizing that the officer’s observation may not reflect the gender specified on the person’s identification
    • Cisgender man/boy
    • Cisgender woman/girl
    • Transgender man/boy
    • Transgender woman/girl
    • Nonbinary person
  • “Perceived or Known Disability of Person Stopped” refers to the officer’s perception that the person stopped displayed signs of one or more of the following conditions; the officer’s knowledge that the person stopped has one or more of the following conditions because the person stopped so advised the officer; or the officer’s prior knowledge that the person stopped had one or more of the following conditions.
    • Deafness or difficulty hearing
    • Speech impairment or limited use of language
    • Blind or limited vision
    • Mental health condition
    • Intellectual or developmental disability, including dementia
    • Other disability
    • None
  • "Actions Taken During Stop" refers to the actions the officer completed during the stop
    • Asked for consent to search person
    • Asked for consent to search property
    • Asked for identification of stopped persons passenger
    • Asked whether the person is on parole, probations, PRCS, or some other form of mandatory supervision
    • Canine used to search for, locate, and/or detect contraband
    • Curbside detention
    • Field sobriety test conducted
    • Frisk/past search of the persons outer clothing was conducted
    • None
    • Patrol car detention
    • Person photographed
    • Person removed from vehicle by order
    • Property was seized
    • Ran name of stopped persons passenger
    • Search of person was conducted
    • Search of property was conducted
    • Vehicle impounded
    • Baton or other impact weapon drawn
    • Baton or other impact weapon used
    • Chemical spray used
    • Electronic control device pointed at person or sparked
    • Electronic control device used in dart-mode
    • Electronic control device used in drive-stun mode
    • Firearm discharged
    • Firearm pointed as person
    • Firearm unholstered
    • Handcuffed or flex cuffed
    • Impact projectile discharged or used
    • Impact projectile weapon pointed as person
    • Officer's canine bit or held person
    • Officer's canine removed from vehicle or used to search
    • Person removed from vehicle by physical contact
    • Physical compliance tactics and techniques
    • Use of vehicle in apprehension of stopped person
  • "Search Rates" refers to the number of people searched sorted by perceived gender when an officer reports an action of "search of person was conducted" or "search of property was conducted".
  • "Discovery Rates" refers to any items discovered during a search sorted by perceived gender unless the option of "none" was reported.
  • “Result of Stop” refers to the outcome of the stop.
    • No action
    • Verbal Warning
    • Written Warning
    • Citation for infraction
    • In-field cite and release
    • Custodial arrest pursuant to outstanding warrant
    • Custodial arrest without warrant
    • Field interview card completed
    • Noncriminal transport or caretaking transport. This includes transport by an officer, transport by ambulance, or transport by another agency.
    • Contacted parent/legal guardian or other person legally responsible for the person.
    • Psychiatric hold (pursuant to Welfare & Institutions Code sections 5150 and/or 5585.20)
    • Contacted U.S. Department of Homeland Security (e.g., Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection)
